question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.
Gradual recovery of health and strength
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Convalescence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Convalescence" means the gradual recovery of health and strength after illness or injury. (बीमारी के बाद धीरे-धीरे स्वास्थ्य लाभ)
◦ Example: After the surgery, she spent two weeks in convalescence before returning to work.

• It comes from the Latin convalescere, meaning "to grow strong", and is commonly used for the recovery period following sickness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Potency (शक्ति): The state of being powerful or strong in effect, especially of a drug or argument; it has nothing to do with recovering health.

• Option 3: Benefaction (परोपकार): An act of doing good, or a charitable donation given to help someone.

• Option 4: Rejuvenation (पुनर्जीवन/यौवन वापस लाना): The process of making someone or something look or feel younger or more vital again — close in idea but not specific to recovering from illness.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused one-word substitutes: Recuperation (also means recovery from illness, near-synonym of convalescence), Recovery, Rehabilitation (restoring someone to normal life after illness/imprisonment/addiction).

• Do not confuse Convalescence (recovering health) with Convenience (suitability/ease) — the spellings look similar but the meanings are unrelated.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
The teacher could judge that his intentions were _________, (nefarious) so he was not stopped from entering the hall.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. pious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given word "nefarious" means wicked, evil, or criminal. (दुष्ट/पापी)

• Since the sentence says the teacher judged that his intentions were the opposite of nefarious — and "so he was not stopped from entering the hall" confirms this positive judgement — the blank needs an ANTONYM of nefarious.

• "Pious" means devoutly religious, virtuous, and morally upright, which is the direct opposite of wicked/nefarious. (धर्मनिष्ठ/सदाचारी)
◦ Example: The pious old man never missed his morning prayers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: traitorous (गद्दार जैसा): Guilty of betrayal or treachery — this is a synonym of nefarious, not an antonym.

• Option 3: envious (ईर्ष्यालु): Feeling jealous of someone; unrelated in meaning to nefarious, and not its opposite.

• Option 4: perfidious (विश्वासघाती): Deceitful and untrustworthy — again a synonym of nefarious (both mean "wicked/treacherous"), not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of nefarious: villainous, iniquitous, heinous, vile, depraved.

• Other antonyms of nefarious: virtuous, honourable, righteous, upright, noble.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Aggreement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the word is "Agreement" — a single "g" — meaning a negotiated and typically legally binding arrangement between parties.

• The option given, "Aggreement", incorrectly doubles the letter "g", which is a common spelling mistake for this word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Arbitrary" is spelt correctly — meaning based on random choice rather than a reason or system.

• Option 2: "Favourite" is spelt correctly (British spelling, with "our"; the American spelling is "favorite").

• Option 4: "Conviction" is spelt correctly — meaning a firm belief, or a formal declaration of guilt.

NOTE

• Words that are frequently misspelt by doubling or dropping a letter incorrectly: Agreement (not Aggreement), Recommend (double "m", single "c"), Occurrence (double "c", double "r"), Embarrass (double "r", double "s"), Harass (single "r", double "s").

• As a memory aid: "Agree" + "ment" = Agreement — think of the base word "agree" (single g) before adding the suffix.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
On the ball
option_1: Doing a job in a slow and incorrect manner
option_2: Doing a job in a quick and competent manner
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Doing a job in a quick and competent manner.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "On the ball" means alert, attentive, and quick to understand and act — i.e., doing a job in a quick and competent manner. (सतर्क और कुशल होना)
◦ Example: Our new manager is really on the ball; she replies to every client query within minutes.

• The idiom originates from ball games (such as football), where a player who is "on the ball" is closely following the ball and reacting swiftly and skilfully to it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Doing a job in a slow and incorrect manner: This is the opposite of the idiom's actual meaning; "on the ball" specifically implies speed and competence, not slowness or error.

• Option 3: Playing with a ball: This is a literal, not idiomatic, reading of the phrase and is incorrect.

• Option 4: Exercising using a ball: Again a literal misreading; the idiom has nothing to do with physical exercise.

NOTE

• Other sports-derived idioms common in SSC exams: "To keep the ball rolling" (to maintain momentum/progress), "The ball is in your court" (it is now your turn to act/decide), "To drop the ball" (to make a mistake or fail to do something expected).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
My students / had expect / guidance from my end.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. had expect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the Past Perfect Tense, signalled by the auxiliary "had".

• Rule — Past Perfect Tense structure: Subject + had + V3 (past participle) + Object.

• Here, "had" is followed by "expect", the base form (V1) of the verb, which is grammatically wrong. It must be replaced by the past participle "expected" (V3), giving the correct form "had expected".
◦ Corrected sentence: My students had expected guidance from my end.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "guidance from my end" is grammatically correct as it stands — a normal noun phrase acting as the object.

• Option 3: "My students" is a correct, error-free subject phrase.

• Option 4: "No error" is incorrect because the sentence does contain an error, in the verb form after "had".

NOTE

• With the auxiliary "had" (Past Perfect), the main verb must always be in its third form (V3) — e.g., had gone, had eaten, had expected — never the base form (V1).

• Commonly tested irregular V3 forms in SSC error-spotting: expect→expected (regular), go→gone, eat→eaten, see→seen, write→written, break→broken.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Capable of being bent or pulled into different shapes
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ductile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Ductile" means capable of being bent, drawn out, or pulled into different shapes (especially of metals) without breaking. (तन्य/लचीला)
◦ Example: Gold and copper are highly ductile metals, which is why they can be drawn into thin wires.

• The word comes from the Latin ducere, meaning "to lead/draw", referring to a material's ability to be "drawn out" into new shapes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Lithe (मोड़दार/फुर्तीला): Used for a person's or animal's body — moving and bending easily and gracefully; not used for materials being reshaped.

• Option 2: Willowy (लचीला और पतला): Describes a person as tall, slim, and graceful — again describes physical build, not the property of a material being shaped.

• Option 4: Lissome (फुर्तीला): Means slim and graceful in movement, typically describing a dancer's body — close to "lithe" but not about a material's capacity to be shaped.

NOTE

• Do not confuse Ductile (can be drawn into wire/shape) with Malleable (can be hammered/pressed into a shape) — both describe workable metals but through different processes.

• Other body-related flexibility words often confused in SSC: Lithe, Lissome, Supple, Willowy, Nimble — all describe graceful/flexible people, not materials.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
He didn't eat a single morsel of food at his daughter's wedding.
option_1: A single morsel of food is not eaten by him at his daughter's wedding.
option_2: A single morsel of food was not eaten by him at his daughter's wedding.
option_3: A single morsel of food can not be eaten by him at his daughter's wedding.
option_4: A single morsel of food was not being eaten by him at his daughter's wedding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A single morsel of food was not eaten by him at his daughter's wedding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "He didn't eat a single morsel of food..." is a negative sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense (Negative):
◦ Active: Subject + did not + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + not + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "a single morsel of food" becomes the subject; since it is singular, the auxiliary is "was"; the verb "eat" becomes the past participle "eaten"; and "he" becomes the agent "by him".
◦ Passive: A single morsel of food was not eaten by him at his daughter's wedding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "is not eaten" is Simple Present Tense passive, which does not match the Simple Past Tense of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "can not be eaten" changes the meaning to expressing inability/possibility, which is not present in the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "was not being eaten" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

NOTE

• With negative sentences, the word "not" is placed immediately after the auxiliary verb (was/were) in the passive voice, exactly as it followed "did" in the active voice.

• Time/place expressions like "at his daughter's wedding" remain unchanged in position at the end of the sentence during active-to-passive conversion.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
My teacher accepted my excuse for being late.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rejected.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "accepted" means agreed to receive or believe something as satisfactory or true. (स्वीकार किया)

• Its antonym is "Rejected", meaning dismissed as unsatisfactory or refused to accept. (अस्वीकार किया)
◦ Example: The teacher rejected his excuse and marked him late.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Trusted (भरोसा किया): Means to have confidence in someone; it is close in spirit to "accepted" rather than its opposite.

• Option 3: Agreed (सहमत हुआ): Means to concur or consent, which is essentially a synonym of "accepted", not an antonym.

• Option 4: Believed (विश्वास किया): Means to accept something as true; again a synonym-type word, not the opposite of "accepted".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "accept": agree to, consent to, approve, acknowledge, embrace.

• Other antonyms of "accept": refuse, decline, reject, deny, repudiate.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A large cage, building, or enclosure to keep birds
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Aviary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Aviary" means a large cage, building, or enclosure in which birds are kept. (पक्षीशाला/पक्षियों का बाड़ा)
◦ Example: The zoo's new aviary houses over fifty species of exotic birds.

• It comes from the Latin avis, meaning "bird" (the same root as "aviation").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Burrow (बिल): A hole or tunnel dug by a small animal (such as a rabbit or fox) as a dwelling — used by land animals, not birds.

• Option 3: Apiary (मधुमक्खी पालन गृह): A place where bees are kept, especially a collection of beehives — commonly confused with "Aviary" because of the similar spelling, but it refers to bees, not birds.

• Option 4: Dormitory (शयनकक्ष): A large bedroom for several people, typically in an institution such as a school or hostel — unrelated to birds.

NOTE

• Frequently confused animal-enclosure words in SSC: Aviary (birds), Apiary (bees), Stable (horses), Kennel (dogs), Sty (pigs), Aquarium (fish), Vivarium (reptiles/small creatures).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Disability was viewed as God's retribution for wickedness in the past.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. punishment for wrongdoing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment "retribution for wickedness" means punishment given as a consequence of doing something wrong or evil.

• "Retribution" = punishment inflicted in return for a wrong committed; "wickedness" = evil or immoral behaviour. Together, the phrase means the disability was seen (wrongly, in the past) as a deserved punishment for wrongdoing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "revenge for legal works" distorts the meaning — retribution is not "revenge for legal works"; this phrase does not make logical sense in context.

• Option 3: "payback for doing help" is incorrect because "wickedness" refers to wrongdoing, not to "doing help" — this reverses the intended meaning.

• Option 4: "fine for misbehaviour" narrows the meaning incorrectly to a monetary fine, whereas "retribution" refers to punishment in a broader, often moral or religious sense, not specifically a fine.

NOTE

• Words related to "retribution": requital, retaliation, vengeance, punishment, comeuppance.

• Words related to "wickedness": sin, vice, immorality, wrongdoing, iniquity — all imply morally bad behaviour.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation.
I was very excited about my new assignment. I sent the email without the required attachment. What have I done?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Jumped the gun.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To jump the gun" means to act too hastily, or to do something before the proper or right time, without adequate preparation. (जल्दबाज़ी में या समय से पहले कुछ करना)
◦ Example: He jumped the gun by announcing the results before they were officially confirmed.

• In the given situation, the person was "very excited" and sent the email "without the required attachment" — i.e., acted too quickly, before making sure everything was ready — which is exactly what "jumped the gun" describes.

• The idiom originates from athletics, where a runner who starts before the starting gun is fired is said to have "jumped the gun".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Shook a leg (जल्दी करना): Means to hurry up or move quickly — it describes speed, not the mistake of acting prematurely/incompletely.

• Option 2: As swift as an eagle: A simile meaning "very fast"; it describes speed of action, not the error of missing a required step.

• Option 4: Tested the waters (स्थिति का अंदाज़ा लगाना): Means to cautiously try something out before committing fully — the opposite of acting hastily, so it does not fit this situation.

NOTE

• Other idioms about acting too soon or without thought: "To put the cart before the horse" (to do things in the wrong order), "To act in haste", "To rush into things".

• Idioms about acting cautiously (the opposite sense): "To test the waters", "To play it safe", "To look before you leap".

question:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank.
The villagers kept the _________ out, to collect the rain water.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cruse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "cruse" is a small earthenware pot or vessel used for holding liquids such as water, oil, or wine.

• In the sentence, "The villagers kept the cruse out, to collect the rain water" makes complete sense, since a cruse is precisely the kind of container used to collect and store water.

• This question tests homonyms/homophones — words that sound alike (or are spelt similarly) but differ in meaning — so the correct option must fit the sense of the sentence, not just the sound.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "crus" is an anatomical term referring to the leg, specifically the part between the knee and the ankle — it has no connection with collecting water.

• Option 3: "crews" refers to groups of people who work together, such as a ship's crew — it cannot be "kept out" to collect rainwater.

• Option 4: "cruise" means a leisure voyage on a ship — it sounds close to "cruse" but is unrelated in meaning to a water-collecting vessel.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused homophone sets tested in SSC: cruse/cruise/crews, desert/dessert, stationary/stationery, principal/principle, council/counsel.

• Always decide such answers by checking which word makes logical sense in the sentence, not merely by how similar the words sound.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The workers had eaten all the pastries before the day broke.
option_1: All the pastries were being eaten by the workers before the day broke.
option_2: All the pastries had been eaten by the workers before the day broke.
option_3: All the pastries have been eaten by the workers before the day broke.
option_4: All the pastries are being eaten by the workers before the day broke.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. All the pastries had been eaten by the workers before the day broke.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active sentence "The workers had eaten all the pastries..." is in the Past Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Past Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + had + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "all the pastries" becomes the subject; the auxiliary becomes "had been"; the verb "eaten" (already V3) is retained; and "the workers" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: All the pastries had been eaten by the workers before the day broke.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "were being eaten" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Past Perfect Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "have been eaten" is the passive form of the Present Perfect Tense, which does not match the past-tense context ("before the day broke").

• Option 4 is incorrect because "are being eaten" is the passive form of the Present Continuous Tense, which is entirely the wrong time frame.

NOTE

• The Past Perfect Tense is used for an action completed before another past action/time — here, the pastries were eaten before the day broke, which is a classic Past Perfect context.

• Passive auxiliary pattern to remember: Present Perfect → has/have been, Past Perfect → had been, Future Perfect → will have been.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Both, Ratan and Moti were idlers and did not work.
B. Their wives had introduced order and industry in the house.
C. Ratan and Moti's wives would work hard and would earn the bread for their family.
D. This made them lazier.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ACBD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence A — "Both, Ratan and Moti were idlers and did not work" — makes the best opening as it introduces the two main characters and their central trait (idleness), which the rest of the paragraph builds on.

• Sentence C logically follows A, since it introduces a contrast: while the men were idlers, "Ratan and Moti's wives would work hard and would earn the bread for their family".

• Sentence B follows C, elaborating on the result of the wives' hard work: "Their wives had introduced order and industry in the house".

• Sentence D concludes the paragraph, with "This" referring back to the wives managing everything, which "made them" (the husbands) "lazier" — a logical cause-and-effect ending.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 (ACBD).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (CDAB) is incorrect because it opens with C, which refers to "Ratan and Moti's wives" before the men (Ratan and Moti) and their idleness have even been introduced by sentence A.

• Option 2 (ABDC) is incorrect because it places D ("This made them lazier") immediately after B, before C has explained what the wives actually did (worked hard and earned the bread) — the cause-effect link breaks down.

• Option 3 (BADC) is incorrect because it opens with B, which uses the pronoun "Their wives" — but whose wives is unclear until sentence A introduces Ratan and Moti first.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always locate the sentence that introduces the subject/characters without relying on a pronoun (like "their", "this", "it") — that sentence is almost always the opening line.

• Track cause-and-effect and contrast markers (such as "This made them...") — they usually signal the concluding sentence of the paragraph.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The investment scheme had been a scam all along.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Swindle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "scam" means a dishonest or fraudulent scheme intended to cheat people, especially of money. (धोखाधड़ी)

• "Swindle" carries the same meaning — a fraudulent scheme to cheat someone out of money or property. (ठगी)
◦ Example: The pyramid investment turned out to be an elaborate swindle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Plain (सरल/स्पष्ट): Means simple, clear, or not elaborate — unrelated in meaning to a fraudulent scheme.

• Option 3: Failure (असफलता): Means lack of success — a scam may ultimately fail, but "failure" itself does not carry the sense of deliberate fraud/deception.

• Option 4: Successful (सफल): Means achieving a desired result — this is nearly the opposite in tone of a fraudulent "scam".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "scam": fraud, con, hoax, racket, sham, deception.

• Common related word forms: swindler (a person who commits fraud), scammer, con artist.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The first is the herbalist, who generally enjoys the prestige and reputation of being the real traditional medical professional.
B. Over the years, I have come to distinguish three types of medical practitioners in African societies and to classify the extent to which each uses medicinal plants.
C. Thirdly, the witch doctor, the practitioner who is credited with the ability to intercept the evil deeds of a witch.
D. The second group represents the divine healers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BADC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence B is the best opening, as it sets up the whole paragraph's framework: "I have come to distinguish three types of medical practitioners in African societies..." — introducing the topic of "three types" that the rest of the sentences describe.

• Sentence A logically follows, introducing the first type: "The first is the herbalist...".

• Sentence D follows next, introducing the second type: "The second group represents the divine healers".

• Sentence C concludes the sequence, introducing the third type: "Thirdly, the witch doctor...".

• The paragraph therefore follows the natural numerical order first → second → third, matching B-A-D-C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 (BADC).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BDAC) is incorrect because it places D ("the second group") before A ("the first is the herbalist"), breaking the natural first-second-third sequence.

• Option 3 (CBAD) is incorrect because it opens with C ("Thirdly, the witch doctor..."), introducing the third type before the "three types" framework of sentence B has even been established.

• Option 4 (ACDB) is incorrect because it opens with A ("The first is the herbalist") without first establishing, as B does, that there are three types of practitioners being discussed.

NOTE

• When a paragraph enumerates items (first, second, third / firstly, secondly, thirdly), always order the sentences to match that explicit numerical sequence.

• The sentence that announces the total count or category (here, "three types of medical practitioners") is almost always the topic sentence and should come first.

question: Identify the sentence with correct spellings.
option_1: Rahul was ashamed of biheving so badly.
option_2: Rahul was ashamed of bihaving so badly.
option_3: Rahul was ashamed of beehaving so badly.
option_4: Rahul was ashamed of behaving so badly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Rahul was ashamed of behaving so badly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "behaving" — from the base verb "behave" (to conduct oneself in a particular way) + the suffix "-ing".

• Spelling key: BE + HAVE + ING → behave drops the silent "e" before adding "-ing", giving behaving. There is only one "e" after "b" and no doubling of any letter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "biheving" is incorrect — the letters have been jumbled/altered from the correct "behaving".

• Option 2: "bihaving" is incorrect — the first syllable is wrongly spelt "bi" instead of "be".

• Option 3: "beehaving" is incorrect — it wrongly doubles the "e" to "bee", which changes the sound and is not the correct form of "behave".

NOTE

• When adding "-ing" to a verb ending in a silent "e", the "e" is normally dropped: behave → behaving, write → writing, come → coming.

• Other commonly misspelt "-ing" forms in SSC exams: beginning (double "n"), occurring (double "r"), arguing (drop the "e" from argue).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
One of these / boxes have / the portrait / of the heiress.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. boxes have.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "One of these boxes". In the structure "One of + plural noun", the actual subject is "One", which is singular — the plural noun ("boxes") is only part of a prepositional phrase describing which group "one" belongs to.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject takes a singular verb. Since the subject here is "One" (singular), the verb must be "has", not "have".

• Corrected sentence: One of these boxes has the portrait of the heiress.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "of the heiress" is a correct, error-free prepositional phrase.

• Option 3: "the portrait" is a correct, error-free noun phrase acting as the object.

• Option 4: "One of these" is grammatically correct on its own — the singular pronoun "One" followed by "of these" is a standard construction; the actual error lies in the verb that follows it in the next segment.

NOTE

• The structure "One of the + plural noun + singular verb" is a frequently tested SSC rule — e.g., "One of the students has submitted the assignment," not "have submitted".

• Similar structures that take a singular verb: Each of, Either of, Neither of, Every one of — all followed by a plural noun but requiring a singular verb.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The hunter drew his bow, but only managed to sever the paw of the wolf before the wolf ran off.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ramify.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "to sever" means to divide or separate something by cutting. (काटकर अलग करना)

• Among the given options, "ramify" carries the closest sense of dividing or splitting into separate parts/branches, which aligns with the core idea of "severing" (dividing) the wolf's paw from its body. (शाखाओं में विभाजित होना)
◦ Example: The old injury caused the nerve to ramify, affecting movement in the paw.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: join (जोड़ना): Means to connect or unite two things — this is the direct opposite of "sever" (which means to separate), so it cannot be a synonym.

• Option 2: mix (मिलाना): Means to combine different things together — unrelated to the idea of cutting/separating a single part.

• Option 4: bind (बांधना): Means to tie or fasten together — again the opposite sense of "sever", since binding joins things rather than dividing them.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "sever": cut off, cleave, sunder, detach, disconnect, split.

• Antonyms of "sever" (words meaning to join/unite): join, bind, connect, unite, attach — useful to recognise, since SSC often mixes synonym and antonym-type distractors in the same option set.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
The old port was abandoned a long ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Kept.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "abandoned" means given up completely; deserted or left permanently. (छोड़ दिया गया)

• Its antonym is "Kept", meaning retained, maintained, or continued to be used/looked after, which is the direct opposite of abandoning something. (बनाए रखा)
◦ Example: Despite the recession, the old lighthouse was kept in operation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Quit (छोड़ना): Means to stop doing something or leave a place — this is close in meaning to "abandoned", not its opposite.

• Option 2: Shortened (छोटा किया गया): Means made shorter or briefer — unrelated to the idea of leaving/retaining a place.

• Option 4: Rashed: Not a standard English word carrying a meaning opposite to "abandoned", and so cannot function as its antonym here.

NOTE

• Other antonyms of "abandoned": retained, maintained, occupied, preserved, sustained.

• Other synonyms of "abandoned": deserted, forsaken, relinquished, discarded, vacated.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The world is going through a deep recession. At such a time, one thing we need in abundance is jobs for the semi-skilled and unskilled. This is the only way in which equal (1)_________ of wealth can take place. The healthcare industry is ideally poised to occupy this position. The IT industry hires people from the upper-middle strata and rich families, usually engineers, (2)_________ the health care industry hires nurses, to the tune of eighty per cent of the jobs created, from the lower economic strata. Global health care is a 4.5-trillion rupee industry, second only to the agro industry. Even then, health care (3)_________ only eight per cent of the world's population. Policymakers should look at the health care industry as not only an industry which addresses pain but also as one which can (4)_________ the economy. The last century was driven by machines that addressed human toil and it is strongly believed that this century will be driven by health care. This, however, will only happen if policy makers make a conscious effort to (5)_________ the right policies in place soon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. distribution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states that jobs for the semi-skilled and unskilled are **"the only way in which equal ________ of wealth can take place." The word needed must express the idea of wealth being shared out or allocated** among people.

• "Distribution" means the action of sharing something out among a number of recipients, which correctly completes the phrase "equal distribution of wealth" — a standard collocation used in economics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "spending" means using money to buy things — this does not fit the idea of wealth being shared equally among people.

• Option 3: "partition" means division, typically of land or territory (e.g., the Partition of India) — it does not collocate naturally with "wealth" in this economic sense.

• Option 4: "earning" refers to the act of making money through work — it does not express the idea of wealth being shared equally across society.

NOTE

• "Equal distribution of wealth/income" is a standard fixed collocation frequently used in economics and current-affairs passages — remember it as a set phrase.

• Related terms often tested together: redistribution (a second, later sharing-out), distribution channel, wealth disparity.

The world is going through a deep recession. At such a time, one thing we need in abundance is jobs for the semi-skilled and unskilled. This is the only way in which equal (1)_________ of wealth can take place. The healthcare industry is ideally poised to occupy this position. The IT industry hires people from the upper-middle strata and rich families, usually engineers, (2)_________ the health care industry hires nurses, to the tune of eighty per cent of the jobs created, from the lower economic strata. Global health care is a 4.5-trillion rupee industry, second only to the agro industry. Even then, health care (3)_________ only eight per cent of the world's population. Policymakers should look at the health care industry as not only an industry which addresses pain but also as one which can (4)_________ the economy. The last century was driven by machines that addressed human toil and it is strongly believed that this century will be driven by health care. This, however, will only happen if policy makers make a conscious effort to (5)_________ the right policies in place soon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. whereas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contrasts two facts: the IT industry hires engineers from the upper-middle/rich strata, **________** the health care industry hires nurses from the lower economic strata.

• "Whereas" is a contrastive conjunction used to compare two differing facts or situations, exactly the relationship being expressed between the IT industry's hiring pattern and the health care industry's hiring pattern.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "unless" introduces a condition ("except if") — there is no conditional relationship between the two clauses here.

• Option 3: "unlike" is a preposition, not a conjunction, and cannot correctly join two independent clauses in this way without altering the sentence structure.

• Option 4: "despite" is also a preposition used to show something happens in spite of an obstacle — it does not fit the simple contrast being made between two parallel facts here.

NOTE

• "Whereas", "while", and "on the other hand" are commonly used to show contrast between two clauses.

• Remember the grammatical distinction: whereas/while are conjunctions (joining two clauses), while despite/unlike/in spite of are prepositions (followed by a noun/noun phrase, not a full clause).

The IT industry hires people from the upper-middle strata and rich families, usually engineers, (2)_________ the health care industry hires nurses, to the tune of eighty per cent of the jobs created, from the lower economic strata. Global health care is a 4.5-trillion rupee industry, second only to the agro industry. Even then, health care (3)_________ only eight per cent of the world's population. Policymakers should look at the health care industry as not only an industry which addresses pain but also as one which can (4)_________ the economy. The last century was driven by machines that addressed human toil and it is strongly believed that this century will be driven by health care. This, however, will only happen if policy makers make a conscious effort to (5)_________ the right policies in place soon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. reaches.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"Even then, health care ________ only eight per cent of the world's population." The verb needed must express the idea of health care's services extending to or covering** a certain percentage of people.

• "Reaches" correctly conveys the sense of coverage/extent — "health care reaches only eight per cent of the population" means its services extend to only that fraction of people.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "cures" means to heal a disease — it does not fit the idea of covering or extending to a percentage of the population.

• Option 2: "visits" implies going to a place temporarily — it does not logically collocate with "only eight per cent of the world's population" in this context.

• Option 4: "calls" does not fit the intended meaning of coverage/extent at all in this context.

NOTE

• In passages about access to services (health care, education, electricity, etc.), the verb "reach(es)" is commonly used to indicate what proportion of people are covered/served.

• Similar collocations: "the scheme reaches millions of farmers", "the internet now reaches remote villages".

The IT industry hires people from the upper-middle strata and rich families, usually engineers, (2)_________ the health care industry hires nurses, to the tune of eighty per cent of the jobs created, from the lower economic strata. Global health care is a 4.5-trillion rupee industry, second only to the agro industry. Even then, health care (3)_________ only eight per cent of the world's population. Policymakers should look at the health care industry as not only an industry which addresses pain but also as one which can (4)_________ the economy. The last century was driven by machines that addressed human toil and it is strongly believed that this century will be driven by health care. This, however, will only happen if policy makers make a conscious effort to (5)_________ the right policies in place soon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. influence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"...as one which can ________ the economy."** The passage argues that health care is not just about addressing pain but can also have a significant positive effect on the economy.

• "Influence" means to have an effect on the character, development, or behaviour of something, which fits the idea that the health care industry can shape/drive the economy — consistent with the passage's closing point that "this century will be driven by health care".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "impede" means to hinder or obstruct progress — this contradicts the passage's overall positive framing of health care's role in the economy.

• Option 2: "persuade" means to convince a person to do or believe something — it is normally used with a person as the object, not an abstract entity like "the economy".

• Option 4: "ascertain" means to find out or discover something for certain — it does not fit the idea of health care actively affecting the economy.

NOTE

• Watch for words that contradict the overall tone of a passage (like "impede" here) — cloze questions often include a near-opposite as a distractor.

• Related word forms: influence (verb/noun), influential (adjective), influencer (noun) — commonly tested together.

The IT industry hires people from the upper-middle strata and rich families, usually engineers, (2)_________ the health care industry hires nurses, to the tune of eighty per cent of the jobs created, from the lower economic strata. Global health care is a 4.5-trillion rupee industry, second only to the agro industry. Even then, health care (3)_________ only eight per cent of the world's population. Policymakers should look at the health care industry as not only an industry which addresses pain but also as one which can (4)_________ the economy. This, however, will only happen if policy makers make a conscious effort to (5)_________ the right policies in place soon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. put.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"...policy makers make a conscious effort to ________ the right policies in place soon." The phrase needed must complete the fixed collocation meaning to implement or establish** policies.

• "Put ... in place" is a standard fixed idiomatic collocation meaning to establish or implement (a system, policy, or arrangement) so that it is ready to operate.
◦ Example: The government must put the right safety measures in place before the factory reopens.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "desire" means to wish for something strongly — it does not collocate with "in place" and does not express the act of implementation.

• Option 2: "cut" means to reduce or remove something — this contradicts the idea of establishing new policies.

• Option 3: "design" means to plan or create something, which is close in idea but does not complete the fixed phrase "________ in place"; only "put" collocates correctly with "in place".

NOTE

• "Put in place" is a very common fixed collocation in formal/policy-related English — memorise it as a set phrase, since "design", "set", or "establish" alone (without "in place") would need different prepositions.

• Similar fixed phrases: "put a plan into action", "put measures in place", "bring a policy into force".
